findings.rationale: Local performance is well below the federation: AUC 0.596 at round 20 (pooled 0.781), ECE 0.159, observed prevalence 0.294 against mean predicted 0.152 (CITL -0.142). A normal-AUC prevalence shift would not drop AUC this far, so the pattern fits flipped outcome labels. Round-1 prevalence was already elevated (0.279 against a pooled ~0.15), so the fault appears to start at round 1. Its updates point against the median (mean cos -0.76) and grow to about 5 to 7 times the median norm from round 3. Per the screening guidance, a wrong-data client trains away from the others, so this is not treated as poisoning. Its local data and performance are abnormal, which rules out a poisoning-only explanation.

Same signature as NE. AUC 0.619 at round 20 (pooled 0.781), ECE 0.147, observed prevalence 0.279 against mean predicted 0.133 (CITL -0.146). The AUC drop with inflated prevalence fits flipped labels rather than a prevalence-only shift. Its updates have mean cos -0.77 and median norm ratio 5.7. Subgroup outcomes are inflated in both sexes (O/E about 2.4 to 2.0) and in several age and income groups, consistent with systematically wrong labels rather than one subgroup. Prevalence is elevated from round 1 (pooled 0.31 for the three flagged clients at round 1).

Same signature as NE and NY. AUC 0.648 at round 20, ECE 0.133, observed prevalence 0.294 against mean predicted 0.162 (CITL -0.132). Prevalence is elevated from round 1 (0.267 at round 1, pooled 0.31 for the three flagged clients). Its updates have mean cos -0.72 and median norm ratio 3.7. Subgroup O/E is inflated in both sexes (about 1.8). The lower AUC is consistent with flipped labels rather than a prevalence shift. Evidence is slightly weaker than NE and NY because its update anomaly is smaller.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients across client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), then confirmed leads with narrower queries. Three clients (NE, NY, SC) show a consistent label-noise signature: AUC of 0.60 to 0.65 against about 0.80 for the rest, observed prevalence about 0.28 to 0.29 against predicted 0.13 to 0.16, CITL around -0.14, elevated prevalence from round 1, and anomalous updates (strongly negative cosine, large norm). Their local data is wrong, so I did not classify them as poisoning. Other leads were spurious: the ND HighChol and NC GenHlth feature outliers did not persist at a narrower query, GU's update anomaly is small-sample noise (z about 3 to 4, normal performance), and the drift and subgroup flags were within noise. The remaining 0 epsilon was spent. No other client met the evidence bar.
